prompt:
Today is November 19, 2026.

Court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit.

We represent: defendant.

Assignment: draft the argument (about 600 words) that a party waives the right to compel arbitration by substantially utilizing the litigation machinery to the prejudice of the other party.

Cite at least six decisions of the Fourth Circuit reported in F.3d, with full Bluebook citations and pin cites. Output only the argument section, with no notes about your process.

Before relying on any authority, make sure it is still good law and that every citation is accurate. Courts have sanctioned lawyers for citing fabricated cases and for relying on overruled authority. Do not cite a case unless you are confident it exists at that citation.
answer:
# ARGUMENT

## [Appellant] Waived Any Right to Compel Arbitration by Substantially Using the Litigation Machinery to [Appellee's] Prejudice.

### A. Waiver turns on the party's own litigation conduct.

Arbitration agreements are enforceable, but the right to enforce one can be lost. A party "may waive its right to arbitrate if it so substantially utilizes the litigation machinery that to subsequently permit arbitration would prejudice the party opposing the stay." *Forrester v. Penn Lyon Homes, Inc.*, 553 F.3d 340, 342 (4th Cir. 2009) (quoting *MicroStrategy, Inc. v. Lauricia*, 268 F.3d 244, 249 (4th Cir. 2001)), *abrogated in part on other grounds by Morgan v. Sundance, Inc.*, 596 U.S. 411 (2022). This Court has applied that rule repeatedly. *See Patten Grading & Paving, Inc. v. Skanska USA Bldg., Inc.*, 380 F.3d 200, 204–05 (4th Cir. 2004); *Am. Recovery Corp. v. Computerized Thermal Imaging, Inc.*, 96 F.3d 88, 95 (4th Cir. 1996); *Rota-McLarty v. Santander Consumer USA, Inc.*, 700 F.3d 690, 701–02 (4th Cir. 2012); *Chorley Enters., Inc. v. Dickey's Barbecue Rests., Inc.*, 807 F.3d 553, 563–64 (4th Cir. 2015).

The Supreme Court has since clarified that waiver of the right to arbitrate is governed by ordinary waiver principles, which focus on whether the party knowingly relinquished the right or acted inconsistently with it. Waiver does not depend on a showing of prejudice. *Morgan*, 596 U.S. at 417–19. Prejudice language in this Court's earlier decisions therefore no longer states an independent requirement. The conduct those decisions identify as waiver remains the touchstone. Here, [Appellant] waived its right under either formulation.

### B. [Appellant] acted inconsistently with any right to arbitrate.

This Court looks to how far the party seeking arbitration has invoked the court's processes. Relevant considerations include the timing and length of the delay, the extent of discovery and motion practice, and whether the party sought a merits ruling from the court. *See Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 205; *Rota-McLarty*, 700 F.3d at 702–04; *Forrester*, 553 F.3d at 343. A party who litigates the merits and invokes arbitration only after an unfavorable result, or after the opposing party has borne the cost of litigation, has chosen a judicial forum. *See Rota-McLarty*, 700 F.3d at 702–04.

[Appellant] did exactly that. [Appellant] [filed the complaint in the district court / answered without asserting arbitration as a defense], and [waited ___ months] before first mentioning arbitration. J.A. __. In that time [Appellant] [served and responded to written discovery, took ___ depositions, and moved for ___ ]. J.A. __. [Appellant] also [sought a ruling on the merits through a motion to dismiss or for summary judgment]. J.A. __. Each step treated the district court as the forum for resolving the dispute. None was consistent with an intention to arbitrate. *See Am. Recovery*, 96 F.3d at 95; *MicroStrategy*, 268 F.3d at 249–51.

### C. [Appellee] was prejudiced.

Even if prejudice remains relevant, this record establishes it. Prejudice exists when the party seeking arbitration allows its opponent to incur the kind of expense and delay that arbitration is meant to avoid, or when it gains information or advantages in litigation that arbitration would not have afforded. *See Rota-McLarty*, 700 F.3d at 702–04; *Forrester*, 553 F.3d at 343; *Patten Grading*, 380 F.3d at 205–06. [Appellee] has spent [$___ / ___ hours] on [discovery, motion practice, and trial preparation]. J.A. __. [Appellant] has also obtained [discovery, rulings, or insight into [Appellee's] litigation strategy] that arbitration procedures would not have allowed. J.A. __. Compelling arbitration now would force [Appellee] to start over and absorb the cost of a second proceeding.

*Chorley*, in which this Court found no waiver, confirms the point. There the party seeking arbitration had acted promptly, and the litigation activity before its motion was limited. 807 F.3d at 563–65. [Appellant]'s conduct is the opposite: delay, sustained merits litigation, and reliance on the court's rulings.

### D. The district court's contrary ruling should be [reversed / affirmed].

Whether a party has waived arbitration is reviewed de novo, with underlying factual findings reviewed for clear error. *See Rota-McLarty*, 700 F.3d at 696–97; *Forrester*, 553 F.3d at 342. Because [Appellant] substantially used the litigation machinery and acted inconsistently with the right it now invokes, it waived any right to compel arbitration.
